description:
src/cache.rs:273-313: every InMemoryCache method uses `self.crl.read().ok()?` / `self.crl.write().ok()?` / `if let Ok(mut guard) = ...`. When the lock is poisoned (a panic in another thread while holding the write lock), get_* returns None forever and put_* / invalidate_* become no-ops. Silently.

Scenario: a panic in any thread that holds the lock (extremely unlikely with InMemoryCache, but a custom impl reusing this pattern in user code is plausible) poisons the lock. Every subsequent revocation check degrades to 'cache miss → full network fetch' silently — correctness preserved, but performance silently degrades to the no-cache baseline, with no error message, no log line, no Debug-output indication. The Debug impl reports 0 entries because it also swallows the poison.

Maintenance consequence: when a deployer reports 'my OCSP cache stopped helping in production, latency p99 doubled', the symptom is invisible. There is no "the cache is poisoned" signal anywhere. The maintainer eventually realizes the lock-poison swallow is in the reference impl and adds logging or panics — that's a future debugging session that could be avoided by either (a) panicking on poison (poisoned lock means a bug elsewhere in the program; failing loud is more useful than failing silent), or (b) using parking_lot which has no poisoning, or (c) documenting that the cache enters 'degraded mode' on poison and exposing a probe method (e.g. `is_degraded() -> bool`).

Recommendation: panic on poison. The standard library's RwLock poisoning model exists to surface bugs; suppressing it is the wrong default for a cache that is supposed to be transparent.
title: InMemoryCache silently swallows lock poisoning into a miss-everything cache
